title: Juara Digital Pandai 2026: A Record Year, Decided Live in Klang
summary: Juara Digital Pandai 2026 brought 200 finalists to one stage in Klang — seven rounds, one live Grand Final. Here's how the day unfolded.
body_markdown:
**On 19 September 2026** , Juara Digital Pandai 2026 did something new. Instead of revealing its champions through an online announcement, it crowned them on stage. The ***Majlis Grand Final Juara Digital Pandai 2026*** took place at **SJKC Wu Teck in Klang** . There, the country’s top young digital learners gathered for a full day of head-to-head competition.


**For the first time, JDP brought its finalists together in person to decide the winners.** This marked a clear step up from how the competition had closed just a year before.


## **What is Juara Digital Pandai?**


**Juara Digital Pandai (JDP) is Pandai’s nationwide academic competition. It runs entirely through the Pandai learning app.** Throughout the competition period, students across Malaysia answer quizzes and collect points known as Rubies. They then climb a national leaderboard, competing against peers from schools all over the country.


The contest welcomes both primary and secondary students. In effect, it turns everyday revision into a friendly national event. Better still, it gives schools, teachers and parents a shared reason to cheer their children on.


## **Juara Digital Pandai 2026 by The Numbers**


So how big was JDP 2026? The competition drew **95,540 students** from **5,556 schools.** Together, they spanned **13 states and federal territories** , all within a four-month window. From that nationwide field, **only 200 students reached the Grand Final — 100 primary and 100 secondary** . In other words, the finalists made up the top 0.2% of everyone who took part. That works out to roughly one finalist for every 478 students who joined.


These finalists came from Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Negeri Sembilan, Kedah, Johor, Perak, Pulau Pinang, Pahang, Melaka, Terengganu, Sabah, Sarawak and Putrajaya — a genuinely national field.


## **A National Record in 2025, Matched in Two-Thirds of The Time**


To measure how far JDP 2026 came, it helps to look back at 2025. That year, the competition gathered ***99,605 students*** from ***5,770 schools over six months*** . That scale set a Malaysia Book of Records entry: the largest student participation in an online academic competition.


**By comparison, JDP 2026 reached 95,540 students from 5,556 schools in just four months.** That equals around **96% of the record** , achieved in a third less time. Month by month, in fact, **sign-ups ran roughly 44% faster** than in the record-setting year.


The 2026 edition also did more with its shorter window. After the four-month competition, the team spent a month preparing something 2025 never had. That something was a live Grand Final — one that crowned its winners in a single day. Back in 2025, champions arrived by announcement. This time, the ceremony crowned them in a hall, in front of an audience, across seven elimination rounds.


## **Inside the Grand Final**


The day began early, with participant registration opening at 8am. Proceedings were opened by the SJKC Wu Teck Diabolo Team — the host school’s own troupe, active since 2014 in developing and promoting the art of diabolo.


The competition itself ran over seven rounds, each split into two phases. In the first, participants answered a 20-question Pandai Quiz in under eight minutes. In the second, they boosted their score through one of ten JDP games, selected at random for each round. Eliminations began from the second round and continued through to the seventh, steadily narrowing the field until only the Top 10 in each category remained.


Reaching that Top 10 was no small feat. With 95,540 students competing nationwide, every finalist who made it that far had effectively outlasted around 4,776 others. Hosting the day were Abang Joe and Abang Syamil, who carried the event through to its closing Award Ceremony. **The Grand Final was also graced by the presence of Pandai ambassador Aqil Zulkiflee.**


## **Recognition That Widened in 2026**


Once the final round concluded and the Top 10 were confirmed, the Award Ceremony recognised achievement across four tiers — presented in order: the SSTP Award for State Education Departments (JPN), the USTP Award for District Education Offices (PPD), the Best School Award, and finally the Best Student Award.


This broader recognition is another way 2026 grew. In 2025, JDP celebrated students and schools. In 2026, it added District Education Offices and State Education Departments to the honours — with Pandai Premium licences flowing back to students in the winning districts and states, so the recognition reached the classrooms behind the champions.


The event was graced by Puan Aniza Binti Kamarulzaman, Pengarah of the Bahagian Sumber Dan Teknologi Pendidikan, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur. Reflecting on initiatives of this kind, she noted:


> *Diharapkan inisiatif ‘challenge’ bermanfaat ke arah pendidikan sebegini dapat memupuk minat murid untuk kekal belajar & turut disantuni semangat oleh pihak guru dengan lebih lagi.*


## **The Prizes**


Across all categories, JDP 2026 awarded **RM34,700 in cash together** with **400 Pandai Premium licences worth RM144,000** , alongside digital hardware, **the JDP 2026 Special Trophy, medals and merchandise.**


### **Student Awards**


The Best Student Award, offered in both primary and secondary categories, gave its champion RM2,000 in cash, with RM1,500 and RM1,000 for the first and second runners-up, and RM300 each for fourth through tenth place — every winner also receiving the JDP 2026 Special Trophy and a certificate. Beyond the Top 10, all Grand Finalists from 11th to 100th place in each category took home a medal, a merchandise pack and a certificate.


### **School and Education-Office Awards**


Schools and education offices were recognised too. The Best School Award granted the top five schools in each category a trophy and a school contribution fund ranging from RM500 to RM3,000, while the USTP (PPD) and SSTP (JPN) awards channelled cash, trophies and substantial Pandai Premium licence packages — including smartboards and smart TVs — to the top-performing district offices and state departments.

## **What Juara Digital Pandai 2026 Showed**


The Malaysia Book of Records entry set in 2025 was a milestone — but JDP 2026 treated it as a starting point rather than a ceiling. Coming within 4% of that record in two-thirds of the time, then gathering its finalists into a single hall, the competition did something its record-setting predecessor never attempted.


There is a quieter achievement in those numbers, too. Reaching national scale in four months instead of six means schools were quicker to sign up, teachers quicker to rally their students, and districts quicker to act. The appetite for this kind of learning is no longer something that has to be built — it is already there. And by placing schools, districts and states on the same stage as students, JDP 2026 made that plain: 5,556 schools do not turn up by chance.


**Ninety-five thousand students began the journey. Two hundred finished it on stage. That is the story JDP 2026 leaves behind — and the standard the next edition will be measured against.**


An event on this scale runs on many hands. Behind every round, every award and every cheer stood the Pandai team. Their months of preparation brought the Grand Final to life. Alongside them, schools, teachers, parents and partners made it matter. **To all of them: thank you.**
